idiom_name: sealed enum/ADT canonical model with exhaustive match, derived tagged codec at the wire edge
implementation_notes: Scala's ADTs are the canonical form: enum Wire (Scala 3) or a sealed trait with case classes plus one decoder per case is the translator set, and match over the sealed hierarchy is exhaustiveness-checked, so routing lives visibly in one place instead of a registry. On the wire side the JSON library derives the discriminator - circe's deriveDecoder/deriveCodec emits and reads a type field for a sealed hierarchy by default, with Configuration or @ConfiguredJsonCodec customizing the key and naming - while non-tagged, positional sources (CSV, fixed width, EDI) still need explicit Decoder instances. A visitor or Translator hierarchy remains justified when translators are pluggable at run time or when several mapping steps must accumulate errors (Either, Validated) instead of failing fast.
code_sketch:
sealed trait Wire                                        // Scala 3: enum Wire derives Codec
case class CsvPayment(raw: String)      extends Wire
case class XmlPayment(document: String) extends Wire

implicit val decodeWire: Decoder[Wire] = deriveDecoder[Wire]   // circe reads the "type" tag

def normalize(json: String): Either[Error, Canonical] =
  decode[Wire](json).map {                                 // router = derived discriminator
    case CsvPayment(raw)      => Canonical.fromCsv(raw)    // exhaustive match
    case XmlPayment(document) => Canonical.fromXml(document)
  }
pitfalls: Exhaustiveness is a warning, not an error, unless the build enables -Xfatal-warnings (with a -Wconf policy): a new wire case otherwise compiles with a MatchError waiting at run time.
Derivation reports an unknown discriminator only as a runtime decode failure, and the default key (type) can collide with a payload field of the same name; configure the discriminator explicitly.
Codec defaults for java.time and BigDecimal (epoch numbers versus ISO strings, scale handling) can shift dates or lose precision if the canonical model is decoded with the wrong implicit.
Type erasure bites list and option payload fields in generic decoders, so keep the canonical ADT non-generic at the boundary and validate cardinality explicitly.
